definitions.explanation: A person who serves in an army. A neutral, general term for military personnel, especially rank-and-file soldiers rather than officers.

examples.japanese: {兵士|へいし}たちが{行進|こうしん}している。
{多|おお}くの{兵士|へいし}が{戦場|せんじょう}で{命|いのち}を{落|お}とした。
examples.english: Many soldiers lost their lives on the battlefield.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{兵士|へいし}たちは{厳|きび}しい{訓練|くんれん}を{受|う}けてから{前線|ぜんせん}に{送|おく}られた。
examples.english: The young soldiers were sent to the front lines after undergoing harsh training.

notes:
A standard, neutral term for soldiers. Used in both historical and modern military contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{兵士|へいし}を{派遣|はけん}する (dispatch soldiers)
・{兵士|へいし}の{訓練|くんれん} (soldier training)
・{負傷|ふしょう}した{兵士|へいし} (wounded soldier)

DISTINCTIONS:
・{兵士|へいし}: soldier (neutral, general — both historical and modern)
・{軍人|ぐんじん}: military person (includes officers, broader than {兵士|へいし})
・{兵隊|へいたい}: soldier (slightly more colloquial, can feel old-fashioned)
・{武士|ぶし}: warrior (specifically Japanese samurai/warrior class)
